title: cli-run: Replace hardcoded RunId(1) with --run-id flag and monotonic counter
description: Bug P0-1. Five CLI call sites hardcode RunId::new(1) for run/run-compiled/bench-run invocations. submit.rs correctly uses SystemTime::now().as_nanos() for unique IDs. Two concurrent vb run invocations would collide on the same RunId, breaking the journal keyspace uniqueness invariant. Master §33.3 (CLI Commands) and §44.15 (Direct API submit/inspect/cancel/list events/answer ask/complete action/fail action/drain trace/health/shutdown) imply every submit/run must allocate a unique RunId. This bead threads an explicit run_id from the parsed Command to the run path, adds --run-id flag (auto-derived when omitted), and adds an AtomicU64 monotonic-counter fallback in submit.rs::generate_submit_run_id. Evidence: run_compiled_runtime.rs:125, bench_run.rs:54, workflow.rs:40,170, bench.rs:27, commands_incident.rs:70,80,91,102,111. Reference: submit.rs:69-71,195-203.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL allocate a unique RunId for every run, run-compiled, and bench-run invocation
THE SYSTEM SHALL use the provided --run-id value as the RunId when present

event_driven.trigger: WHEN the user passes --run-id N on the run/run-compiled/bench-run CLI
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL use RunId(N) as the run identifier and parse N as a u64

event_driven.trigger: WHEN the user omits --run-id on the run CLI
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL derive a unique RunId from the submit path monotonic counter (AtomicU64 fallback after SystemTime::now().as_nanos())

unwanted.condition: IF two vb run invocations land in the same nanosecond
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT collide on the same RunId
unwanted.because: RunId is the Fjall keyspace primary key; collision would silently overwrite prior run data and destroy journal history

unwanted.condition: IF --run-id is provided with a value that does not parse as u64
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT silently default to RunId(1)
unwanted.because: Silent fallback hides a CLI usage error from the operator and corrupts the journal

preconditions: CLI binary velvet-ballistics is built and on PATH
Workflow YAML at the supplied path parses to a valid CompiledWorkflow
postconditions: RunId written to the Fjall keyspace is the explicit --run-id value, OR a fresh value from generate_submit_run_id, OR RunId(1) ONLY when --run-id 1 is explicitly passed
run_compiled_workflow receives run_id: RunId as a function parameter, never reads a hardcoded constant
submit.rs::generate_submit_run_id falls back to an AtomicU64 monotonic counter when SystemTime::now().as_nanos() collides with a prior in-process allocation
invariants: RunId uniqueness: two concurrent CLI invocations produce two distinct RunIds
submit path and run path use the same RunId allocation policy
No .unwrap() / .expect() / panic! on parse failure of --run-id; the CLI exits with a typed ValidationFailed error

happy: cli_run_uses_unique_run_ids_per_invocation: two parallel `vb run foo.yaml` invocations write distinct RunIds to the journal
cli_run_with_explicit_run_id_flag_uses_provided_value: `vb run foo.yaml --run-id 42` writes RunId(42) regardless of clock
submit_and_run_paths_agree_on_run_id: a submit+run pair of the same workflow produces a single journal entry with the same RunId
error: cli_run_with_invalid_run_id_returns_validation_failed: `vb run foo.yaml --run-id notanumber` exits 3 with ValidationFailed message
cli_run_with_negative_run_id_returns_validation_failed: `vb run foo.yaml --run-id -1` exits 3 (u64 underflow is a parse error)
edge: cli_run_with_run_id_zero_writes_run_id_zero: `vb run foo.yaml --run-id 0` writes RunId(0) (valid, not a default sentinel)
cli_run_with_run_id_u64_max_succeeds: `vb run foo.yaml --run-id 18446744073709551615` writes RunId(u64::MAX) without overflow

patterns: Pattern: existing nanos-based RunId allocation in submit.rs (the reference correct implementation)
Pattern: clap derive flags for --run-id with u64 parser (see vb_cli/src/args/patterns.rs)
questions: Should --run-id be available on submit as well, or only on run/run-compiled/bench-run? (Spec says run-path; submit is correct.)
Does the AtomicU64 fallback live in submit.rs::generate_submit_run_id only, or should run path also have one? (Spec says submit fallback; run path delegates.)

security_failures.failure: Operator passes --run-id matching a prior run's ID, overwriting or corrupting journal state
security_failures.prevention: Document --run-id as 'advanced/replay-only'; do not warn loudly because replay tools may legitimately reuse IDs against a fresh DB

usability_failures.failure: User cannot reproduce a flaky run because RunId is non-deterministic across invocations
usability_failures.prevention: Provide --run-id so the same RunId can be passed to replay, inspect, and events subcommands across runs

data_integrity_failures.failure: Two parallel invocations both write RunId(1), silently losing one run's journal events
data_integrity_failures.prevention: Use submit-style nanos + AtomicU64 fallback in run path too, OR explicit --run-id from caller
data_integrity_failures.test_for_it: cli_run_uses_unique_run_ids_per_invocation (50 parallel runs, count distinct RunIds in journal — must be 50)

integration_failures.failure: vb inspect and vb events cannot find a run that was started via `vb run` because no RunHeaderRecord was written
integration_failures.prevention: Pair with P1-13: ensure run path writes WorkflowSourceRecord and RunHeaderRecord (separate bead; P0-1 just fixes the ID allocation)
integration_failures.test_for_it: P1-13 covers this; P0-1 is strictly the ID allocation

similar_implementations: submit.rs nanos allocation is the canonical pattern to copy

apis_that_exist: SystemTime::now().as_nanos() returns u128 (must convert to u64 or use lower 64 bits)
AtomicU64::fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) is the standard monotonic counter primitive
apis_that_do_not_exist: There is no `Command::RunId::derive()` helper — must construct RunId from u64 explicitly
no_placeholder_values: Do NOT use RunId::new(1) as a 'default' value; the default must be a fresh allocation from generate_submit_run_id
Do NOT use 0 as a sentinel for 'uninitialized'; --run-id 0 is a valid explicit value
